summary: Week 6 POC closeout. Redwood and NexaHealth reviewed pilot results (latency P95, throughput, error rates), discussed final tuning steps, clarified success criteria tied to exec approval, and agreed next steps: pricing, security artifacts, exec handoff, and a 72-hour dedicated stress run. Customer has budget conversation internally; legal raised a couple of data retention questions to be answered with documents.
transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-09-02 16:00 UTC | Duration: 49 minutes | Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Maya Patel (Redwood SE), Liam O'Rourke (CSM), Jordan Alvarez (NexaHealth PM), Priya Singh (Director), Marcus Lee (Infra), Anika Rao (Legal)

[00:00] Alex Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate the time. Quick roll call — I see Priya, Jordan, Marcus?
[00:07] Jordan Alvarez: Yeah, here. Sorry, had a hard stop earlier so I joined a bit late.
[00:10] Priya Singh: On my side, thanks Alex.
[00:12] Marcus Lee: Here.
[00:13] Anika Rao: Anika from legal, hi.
[00:15] Maya Patel: Hi, Maya from Redwood SE. I'll do most of the perf walkthrough.
[00:19] Alex Chen: Cool. Goal for today: go through the final POC numbers, confirm success criteria for exec signoff, and align on next steps — pricing + security + a short dedicated run to validate steady state.

[00:35] Jordan Alvarez: That sounds good. We mostly want to know if the performance we saw in week 5 is stable and what the delta is if we go Dedicated vs hosted. Also need the business case numbers for my CFO.

[00:50] Maya Patel: Okay, I'll jump into results. Quick disclaimer — some of the metrics come from the instrumentation agent which sometimes tags tokens differently, so absolute numbers might be off by a few percent, but trends are sound.

[01:05] Maya Patel: P95 latency on the hosted trial averaged 320ms for 512-token prompts under the mixed prompt set; on Dedicated with the same model variant we saw 210ms. Throughput: hosted sustained ~95 rps for bursty workload, Dedicated sustained 300 rps before queueing. Error rate under load peaked at 1.8% on hosted vs 0.4% on Dedicated.

[01:42] Marcus Lee: Those Dedicated numbers look good. Can you remind us what the batching config was? I know you did continuous batching and the KV cache was enabled.

[01:54] Maya Patel: Yes — default continuous batching with a max batch size of 64, dynamic latency SLO set to 250ms for Dedicated testing. KV cache: enabled, prefix caching for repeated session state — that'll be the biggest wins for our chat-based flows. Note: some of the instrumentation labels the KV cache as K-B cache in the dump, sorry for the odd label.

[02:20] Jordan Alvarez: There's a chunk of the exec ask that cares about predictable cost. Can you translate those throughput numbers into cost-per-1k-tokens at the committed tier?

[02:31] Alex Chen: We have an initial committed pricing sheet; I'll send the final numbers but ballpark: Dedicated committed rate reduces token USD cost by ~45% compared to pay-as-you-go hosted for this workload, primarily because of amortized GPU utilization and higher sustained throughput. I'll attach a simpler committed throughput worksheet.

[02:54] Priya Singh: We'll need that in the slide deck for execs. Liam, can you do the business-case slide?

[03:02] Liam O'Rourke: Yep, I can take that, I'll work with Alex on final numbers.

[03:08] Anika Rao: From legal — couple of items on data retention and audit logs. During the trial logs were kept in the Redwood console for 30 days. We need retention options, KMS integration specifics, and a SOC2 artifact.

[03:20] Alex Chen: Understood. We'll send SOC 2 attestation, network diagrams for VPC peering, and a short KMS integration note. Maya will include notes about what data is cached locally vs encrypted at rest.

[03:36] Maya Patel: Right — by default logs are written to the control plane with PII redaction options; KV cache is ephemeral on the Dedicated hosts and can be configured to not persist beyond session TTL. We'll document that.

[03:50] Jordan Alvarez: For success criteria, we proposed: P95 latency <= 250ms, cost-per-1k-tokens <= $X (we'll fill X when we get committed pricing), and error rate < 1%. Can we lock those?

[04:05] Maya Patel: Those are achievable but P95 <= 250ms requires dedicated + tuned batching and the 72-hour stress run to prove steady state, given the real-world distribution of request lengths.

[04:18] Priya Singh: That makes sense. The CFO will want the stress-run numbers before signoff. We can treat the stress run as the gating artifact.

[04:27] Marcus Lee: Regarding security, we'll need to validate HSM/KMS key scoping and confirm that audit logs show per-token request IDs for compliance.

[04:36] Maya Patel: We can provide a small script to verify request IDs in logs; the demo logs we gave earlier included request_id and session_id fields but the exporter sometimes truncates long IDs in CSV — another small artifact to be aware of.

[04:54] Jordan Alvarez: One question: you mentioned fallback model variants if capacity is constrained. In our usage pattern, if Dedicated capacity drops, do we get automatic fallback to hosted and does that impact our SLA or cost assumptions?

[05:08] Alex Chen: Good question. The policy we ran in the pilot was: prefer Dedicated, fallback to hosted for short-lived bursts with explicit throttling. Fallback can be disabled; if enabled, calls may route to hosted which changes cost and latency. For contractual SLAs, we can define failover behavior. We'll include that in the runbook.

[05:34] Anika Rao: Also legal wanted to confirm where logs live when fallback happens — are they split between control planes?

[05:40] Maya Patel: Fallback logs are still ingested into the same tenant console; however, depending on deployment mode, some telemetry might be forwarded from hosted control plane — we'll document retention and residency specifics per your compliance needs.

[06:00] [small crosstalk] Speaker 5: (unclear)

[06:05] Jordan Alvarez: Back to the numbers — Maya, can you summarize the tuning changes you'd recommend we do before the stress run?

[06:12] Maya Patel: Sure. Short list: 1) Increase max batch size to 80 for Dedicated steady-state runs, 2) set dynamic latency SLO to 220ms for interactive flows, 3) enable aggressive prefix caching on session types where prompt templates repeat, 4) lower token output sampling temperature for deterministic evaluation during the run to reduce variance. I'll put exact CLI/config fragments in the note. Also we recommended enabling the 'prefetch kv' flag for sequences with many lookups — it's labeled prefetch in the UI but in logs sometimes shows as pre-fetch which is silly.

[07:05] Marcus Lee: That prefetch thing — will it increase memory footprint on the GPU? We need to make sure our Dedicated pool sizing covers that.

[07:12] Maya Patel: Slight increase, yes—mostly on-host RAM for the cache pointers, not model memory. We'll share numbers: expected ~6–8% overhead for typical sessions.

[07:27] Priya Singh: On the business-case front, if Dedicated reduces cost by ~45%, we need to show net savings after committed monthly fee; Liam, include the committed cost and break-even month.

[07:40] Liam O'Rourke: Will do. I'll assume the committed tier we discussed in the proposal and build out a 12/24 month comparison.

[07:49] Jordan Alvarez: One more item — we ran a small integration test where we saw some tokenization mismatch across our ingestion pipeline and Redwood's tokenizer for edge characters. That caused a couple of prompts to be slightly longer in tokens. Any guidance?

[08:03] Maya Patel: Yes — the tokenizer mismatch happens mostly with non-UTF punctuation in legacy data. We suggest normalizing on the client side or enabling the 'strict-tokenize' flag during the run. We can send a small sanitizer script.

[08:20] Anika Rao: Legal note: we still need a short comms on data residency for EU customers — our legal team wants a statement that data will not be replicated outside region without notice.

[08:31] Alex Chen: We'll include regional residency statements and include options for Private (VPC/on-prem) if you need data to stay entirely inside their cloud tenancy.

[08:42] Jordan Alvarez: Great. So, mechanics for final steps — can we schedule the 72-hour dedicated run for next week and have Redwood own spinning the pool? We will validate and sign off with the CFO after run results.

[08:54] Alex Chen: Yes — Redwood can provision a dedicated pool for the 72-hour run. Need Marcus to share peering window and we need a go/no-go confirmation 48 hours before.

[09:06] Marcus Lee: I'll send peering times and contact for infra ops by EOD Friday.

[09:12] Alex Chen: Perfect. Let's recap — and I'll pull out explicit owners.

[09:18] Alex Chen: Recap: 1) Redwood sends final committed pricing + throughput worksheet (Alex) 2) Redwood SE sends perf logs, tuning notes, and config fragments (Maya) 3) Redwood to provision a 72-hour Dedicated run, customer to validate and sign off (Alex/Maya) 4) Redwood to share SOC2, KMS/HSM notes, and network diagrams (Alex) 5) CSM (Liam) to draft exec slide and ROI. Customer owners: Jordan to confirm metric signoff and budget, Marcus to provide peering window, Anika to follow up on retention wording.

[09:50] Priya Singh: That works. If we see the stress run numbers align with the P95 and error targets, we plan to move to contract in two weeks pending legal.

[09:58] Jordan Alvarez: Thanks, all. One last micro point — can you include a short note on fallback cost impact in the pricing doc?

[10:05] Alex Chen: Yes, I'll add a 'failover cost impact' appendix.

[10:10] Liam O'Rourke: I'll schedule the executive sync and share a calendar invite for week of 2025-09-08.

[10:18] Maya Patel: I'll get the tuning docs out tomorrow and include the tokenizer sanitizer.

[10:22] Anika Rao: I'll route the retention questions internally and follow up with specifics.

[10:27] Alex Chen: Great — thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email with links to artifacts.

[10:33] [meeting ends]

Notes: transcription includes imperfect labels and occasional truncation in logs; some product names are abbreviated (e.g., Dedicated -> Ded, KV -> K-B in logs). References: pricing worksheet (link to be shared), SOC2 attestation (doc), perf logs (artifact)
